lessons.title: Oral cavity and swallowing
lessons.summary: The mouth begins mechanical processing and salivary digestion.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The hard palate forms the anterior bony roof, the soft palate is posterior and muscular, and the tongue occupies the floor of the mouth.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The parotid duct opens near an upper molar, the submandibular duct opens beside the lingual frenulum, and sublingual ducts open in the floor.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The pharynx follows the oral cavity and the esophagus follows the pharynx; salivary glands are accessory organs rather than segments of the alimentary canal.

lessons.title: Stomach regions
lessons.summary: Stomach regions mix food and begin protein digestion.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The cardia surrounds the esophageal entry, the fundus rises above it, the body is the broad central region, and the pyloric antrum and canal lead to the pylorus.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Rugae are folds of the stomach lining that flatten with distension; gastric pits open into glands containing parietal and chief cells.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The pylorus is the distal region and the pyloric sphincter is its muscular outlet; rugae are not small-intestinal villi.

lessons.title: Small intestine and mucosa
lessons.summary: The three small-intestinal regions absorb digested nutrients.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Brunner glands are submucosal duodenal glands, whereas intestinal crypts extend into the mucosa.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The duodenum, jejunum, and ileum differ in mucosal and submucosal landmarks along the small intestine.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Do not label a submucosal duodenal gland as an intestinal crypt.

lessons.title: Large intestine
lessons.summary: The large intestine reclaims water and conducts fecal material.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Haustra and taeniae coli are gross landmarks of the colon; the anal sphincters mark the terminal outlet.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Taeniae coli shorten the colon wall and contribute to its haustrated contour.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Haustra are colonic pouches, not small-intestinal villi.

lessons.title: Accessory digestive organs
lessons.summary: Bile and pancreatic secretions reach the duodenum through connected ducts.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Hepatic lobules are centered on a central vein and contain portal triads at their periphery; pancreatic acini surround ducts.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Portal triads and hepatic sinusoids organize blood flow through the liver lobule, while pancreatic acini drain toward the pancreatic duct.
In cirrhosis, scar tissue replaces healthy liver tissue and disrupts the usual lobular arrangement and blood passages.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
A hepatic sinusoid is a vascular channel, not a bile duct; pancreatic islets are endocrine regions among exocrine acini.

lessons.title: Digestive wall layers
lessons.summary: Wall layers organize secretion, absorption, vessels, and propulsion.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
From lumen outward, the wall is mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa, and serosa where covered by peritoneum; mucosa includes epithelium, lamina propria, and muscularis mucosae.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Circular then longitudinal layers comprise the muscularis externa, while submucosa contains larger vessels and connective tissue.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Muscularis mucosae is a thin mucosal layer, not the muscularis externa; serosa is the outer covering, not submucosa.

lessons.title: Digestive histology
lessons.summary: Specialized cells and surfaces identify digestive tissue slides.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Villi and microvilli project from small-intestinal mucosa; enterocytes line the surface, goblet cells are pale mucous cells, and Paneth cells sit at crypt bases.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Gastric pits lead to glands with parietal and chief cells, while hepatocytes are arranged in plates around hepatic sinusoids.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Villi are mucosal projections and crypts are invaginations; microvilli are apical cell specializations, not whole villi.

lessons.title: Peritoneal relationships
lessons.summary: Peritoneal folds suspend, connect, and protect abdominal organs.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The mesentery is a double peritoneal fold associated with small intestine; the greater omentum hangs from the greater curvature and the lesser omentum spans liver to stomach and duodenum.
In the transverse section, the parietal layer lines the body wall, whereas visceral peritoneum turns onto organ surfaces; the narrow potential space between them is the peritoneal cavity.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
These folds carry vessels, nerves, and lymphatics while connecting abdominal organs and enclosing peritoneal surfaces.
The kidneys lie posterior to the peritoneal cavity; much of the pancreas is also retroperitoneal. Mesenteries are double folds carrying vessels and nerves to suspended viscera.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The greater and lesser omenta are peritoneal folds, not wall layers; mesentery is distinct from serosa covering an organ.
Do not confuse the peritoneal cavity with the lumen of the gut or treat the kidneys as intraperitoneal. This is a schematic section, not a specimen.

lessons.title: Portal circulation
lessons.summary: Absorbed nutrients travel through portal blood to hepatocytes.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The hepatic portal vein enters the liver and distributes toward portal triads; blood then passes through sinusoids toward central veins.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Hepatocytes lie between sinusoidal blood and bile canalicular pathways, allowing portal venous blood to traverse the lobule.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The portal vein carries blood, not bile; the hepatic artery is also part of the portal triad, whereas bile leaves through ducts.

lessons.title: Alimentary canal continuity
lessons.summary: Trace the lumen from mouth to anus without substituting accessory organs.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The lumen proceeds mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, duodenum, jejunum, ileum, cecum, colon, rectum, anal canal, and anus.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The ileocecal valve marks entry into the cecum, and the colon continues as rectum before the anal canal and terminal anus.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Liver, gallbladder, and pancreas are accessory organs and are not traversed by the alimentary lumen.

lessons.title: Kidney regions
lessons.summary: Cortex, medulla, pyramids, and calyces orient the kidney.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The renal hilum opens into the renal sinus, which contains the pelvis, calyces, vessels, and connective tissue. The Gray plate is for gross kidney location and relations, not internal microanatomy.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Cortex surrounds the medulla, while the renal sinus is the internal space continuous with the hilum; kidneys lie beside the aorta and IVC.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The renal sinus is an internal space; the renal pelvis is the urine-collecting funnel within it.

lessons.title: Urinary tract
lessons.summary: The tract conducts, stores, and expels urine.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The detrusor forms the muscular bladder wall and the external urethral sphincter lies distal to the internal sphincter.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Urothelium lines the ureter and bladder, while the detrusor provides the bladder wall muscle.
The prostatic segment of the male urethra runs through the gland below the bladder; enlargement can narrow that passage.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The ureter carries urine to the bladder; the urethra carries it from the bladder to the exterior.

lessons.title: Nephron segments
lessons.summary: Tubular segments modify filtrate.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Filtrate leaves the renal corpuscle for the proximal convoluted tubule, nephron loop, distal convoluted tubule, and collecting duct; the loop has descending and ascending limbs.
Follow blood from the afferent arteriole INTO the glomerular capillaries and OUT by the efferent arteriole; the filtrate enters the capsular space and then the proximal convoluted tubule.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The nephron loop extends toward the medulla, while collecting ducts pass through the medulla to papillary ducts.

The loop descends and returns before fluid reaches the distal nephron and collecting passage. The nearby peritubular network exchanges materials with the tubules; it is a blood route, not the urinary lumen.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
A collecting duct receives fluid from multiple nephrons and is not itself the entire nephron; the nephron loop is not synonymous with a single limb.
A collecting duct contains tubular fluid, not blood. This schematic is not a microscopic section, so do not assign a stain, species, or magnification.

lessons.title: Renal corpuscle
lessons.summary: The corpuscle begins filtration across a specialized barrier.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The glomerulus is a capillary tuft inside the glomerular capsule; podocyte processes cover capillaries and contribute to the filtration membrane.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The filtration membrane lies between glomerular blood and capsular space and includes fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane, and podocyte slit regions.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The glomerulus is vascular and the capsular space is urinary; neither should be labeled as a renal tubule.

lessons.title: Renal vessels
lessons.summary: Vessels branch from hilum toward nephron capillaries.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
From the renal artery, branches pass through segmental and interlobar arteries, arc as arcuate arteries, and radiate through cortex as cortical radiate arteries before afferent arterioles.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The efferent arteriole leaves the glomerulus to form peritubular capillaries or vasa recta; venous return follows cortical radiate veins, arcuate veins, interlobar veins, then the renal vein.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Afferent enters and efferent exits the glomerular tuft; arteries and veins use corresponding named levels but are not interchangeable.

lessons.title: Urinary histology
lessons.summary: Distinct epithelia and cells reveal urinary function.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Urothelium has rounded superficial cells and lines the bladder and ureter; podocytes surround glomerular capillaries, while macula densa cells form a dense patch of distal tubule.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Macula densa, juxtaglomerular cells, and associated vasculature form the juxtaglomerular apparatus; principal and intercalated cells occupy collecting ducts.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Macula densa belongs to the distal tubule, not the collecting duct; podocytes are corpuscle cells, not principal cells.

lessons.title: Urine pathway
lessons.summary: Trace filtrate from corpuscle to the outside.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Urine drains from collecting ducts through papillary ducts, minor and major calyces, renal pelvis, ureter, bladder, and urethra.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The renal pelvis is the funnel within the renal sinus, the ureter enters the bladder at the trigone, and the urethra exits it.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The nephron loop and collecting duct carry tubular fluid, whereas calyces and pelvis carry urine after it leaves the papillary ducts.

lessons.title: Testis and coverings
lessons.summary: Testicular compartments support sperm production and endocrine function.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Tunica vaginalis covers the testis externally, while septa from the tunica albuginea divide it into lobules.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Seminiferous tubules occupy lobules and converge on the rete testis through the testicular mediastinum.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Tunica vaginalis is a serous covering and is distinct from the fibrous tunica albuginea.

lessons.title: Epididymis and duct system
lessons.summary: Sperm mature and travel through connected ducts; the spermatic cord supports the testis and duct.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The route is seminiferous tubule, short straight tubules, rete testis, efferent ductule, epididymal head, body, tail, ductus deferens, ampulla, ejaculatory duct, and urethra.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Short straight tubules connect seminiferous tubules to the rete testis; the epididymis lies along the posterior testis and its tail continues as ductus deferens.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Efferent ductules follow the rete testis, not the seminiferous tubule directly; the ejaculatory duct is not the urethra.

lessons.title: Accessory glands
lessons.summary: Glands add fluids with distinct contributions to semen.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Seminal vesicles lie posterior to the bladder, the prostate surrounds the proximal urethra, and bulbourethral glands lie inferior to the prostate near the membranous urethra.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Seminal-vesicle and ductus-deferens ducts unite as the ejaculatory duct; prostate and bulbourethral secretions enter the urethral route.
Benign prostate enlargement changes the size of the gland surrounding the prostatic urethra; keep gland and urethral lumen distinct.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The testis produces sperm, but accessory glands contribute fluid; the seminal vesicle is a gland, not a storage sac for sperm.

lessons.title: External anatomy
lessons.summary: External structures and scrotal muscle layers protect and position reproductive tissues.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The bulbospongiosus overlies the bulb of the penis and the corpora cavernosa are paired dorsal erectile bodies.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The corpus spongiosum surrounds the spongy urethra and expands distally as the glans.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The dartos is smooth muscle in scrotal tissue; the cremaster is skeletal muscle associated with the spermatic cord.

lessons.title: Spermatogenesis
lessons.summary: Germ cells progress through meiosis and differentiation in seminiferous tubules.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Within seminiferous tubules, spermatogonia lie basally, primary and secondary spermatocytes are more luminal, then spermatids and spermatozoa approach the lumen.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Sertoli cells support germ cells across the blood-testis barrier, and mature sperm leave the seminiferous epithelium toward the rete testis.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
A spermatid is a haploid developing cell and is not yet a spermatozoon; the acrosome and flagellum are parts of the mature sperm cell.

lessons.title: Male reproductive histology
lessons.summary: Supporting, endocrine, germ, and erectile tissues identify male histology.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Seminiferous tubules show germ-cell layers and Sertoli cells; Leydig cells occupy interstitial tissue, while erectile tissue contains vascular spaces.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Peritubular myoid cells surround seminiferous tubules, and the corpus spongiosum surrounds the spongy urethra while corpora cavernosa are paired.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Leydig cells are interstitial rather than intratubular; corpus spongiosum is distinct from the paired corpora cavernosa.

lessons.title: Sperm pathway and support
lessons.summary: Trace sperm while keeping the urethra, cord, and erectile structures distinct from the duct pathway.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Sperm travel from seminiferous tubules through short straight tubules, rete testis, efferent ductules, epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and urethra.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Short straight tubules provide the transition from seminiferous tubules to rete testis; the prostatic urethra follows the ejaculatory duct, then the spongy urethra traverses the penis.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The urethra carries both urinary and reproductive outflow but is not part of the testicular duct system; the pampiniform plexus is vascular.

lessons.title: Ovary and follicles
lessons.summary: The ovary houses follicles and produces oocytes and hormones.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The ovarian hilum is the vascular entry region of the medulla; follicles are concentrated in the cortex.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Follicles progress through cortical stages and the postovulatory corpus luteum may become corpus albicans.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The corpus luteum is a functional postovulatory structure, whereas the corpus albicans is its fibrous remnant.

lessons.title: Uterine tube
lessons.summary: Tube regions guide the oocyte toward the uterus.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
From lateral to medial, the uterine tube has fimbriae at the infundibulum, a broad ampulla, and a narrow isthmus approaching the uterus.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Fimbriae border the ovarian end without enclosing the ovary, and ciliated tubal epithelium helps move material toward the uterine cavity.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The ampulla is wider than the isthmus; the uterine tube is not continuous with the ovary and does not attach directly to its surface.

lessons.title: Uterus and cervix
lessons.summary: Uterine regions and the cervix form the birth canal.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The fundus is the dome above the uterine body; the cervix is the inferior narrowed portion, with an internal os toward the uterine cavity and external os toward the vagina.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The cervical canal connects the uterine cavity to the vagina, and the vaginal fornix surrounds the projecting cervix.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The cervix is part of the uterus, not a separate tube; internal and external os refer to opposite ends of the cervical canal.

lessons.title: Uterine wall
lessons.summary: Wall layers support implantation, cycling, and contraction.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The endometrium has functional and basal strata, and uterine glands extend through its mucosa.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The stratum functionale is shed cyclically while the stratum basale regenerates it; the myometrium forms the contractile wall.
A uterine fibroid is a localized growth of smooth-muscle-rich tissue in or on the uterine wall; distinguish it from the normal endometrial lining.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Perimetrium is the outer serosal covering, not the inner endometrium.

lessons.title: Reproductive support
lessons.summary: Ligaments and folds position the reproductive organs.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The broad ligament is a peritoneal fold; the mesovarium attaches to the ovary, the suspensory ligament carries ovarian vessels, and the ovarian ligament connects ovary to uterus.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The round ligament runs from the uterus toward the labia through the inguinal canal, while the suspensory ligament connects the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The ovarian ligament is not the suspensory ligament: the former connects ovary and uterus, while the latter carries vessels.

lessons.title: Vulva and mammary anatomy
lessons.summary: External genital and mammary structures have distinct landmarks.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The vulva includes mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoris, and vestibule; the greater vestibular glands open into the vestibule.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Mammary lobules drain into lactiferous ducts, which widen as lactiferous sinuses before opening at the nipple; the areola surrounds the nipple.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The vestibule is an external genital space, not the vagina; a mammary lobule is glandular tissue and a lactiferous duct is its drainage passage.

lessons.title: Female reproductive histology
lessons.summary: Follicle stages and epithelia identify reproductive tissue; secretory mammary alveoli are smaller units that drain into larger mammary ducts.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
Ciliated columnar cells of the uterine tube and nonkeratinized squamous cells of the vagina are distinctive slide landmarks.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
Tubal cilia and folds aid oocyte transport, while vaginal epithelium resists abrasion.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
Do not use the general term follicular fluid for the zona pellucida or the corona radiata surrounding the oocyte.

lessons.title: Oocyte pathway
lessons.summary: Trace the oocyte from ovary through the uterine tube and relate the uterus.
recognitionCues: Orient by position, continuity, and distinctive wall or tissue features.
Compare adjacent structures before selecting a label.
The oocyte is released from the ovary near the fimbriae, enters the infundibulum, traverses ampulla and isthmus, and reaches the uterus; the uterine cavity continues through cervix and vagina.
landmarks: Use named boundaries, layers, and connected passages as landmarks.
relationships: Location predicts the structure’s contribution to the organ pathway or function.
The uterine tube is lateral to the uterus and the cervix is the uterine segment that projects into the vagina.
commonConfusions: Do not substitute a neighboring structure or a different tissue layer.
The fimbriae do not form a direct ovarian lumen; the vagina follows the cervix and is not another region of the uterine tube.
